stanzas: My country, my country, my country,
yours are my love and my heart.
My country, my country, my country,
yours are my love and my heart.
Egypt, O mother of the lands,
you are my aim and my desire,
how many favours your Nile has bestowed!
Egypt, you are the most precious pearl,
a white blaze on the forehead of time.
and stay safe in spite of the enemies.
faithful, they keep hold of the reins.
and we are your ransom, O my country.

notes: Romanization: ALA-LC without the dots under letters, with ʿ and ʾ, rendering the words as the vocalised text writes them, including its Egyptian forms: 'Masri' (مَصْرِ, with a, as Egyptians say it), 'fūq' for fawqa, the pausal 'nīlik', 'awlādik' and 'fidākī'.
line 2.4: 'ayādī', literally 'hands', is the classical word for favours or benefactions.
line 3.2: 'ghurrah' is the white blaze on a horse's forehead, hence the finest and most conspicuous thing.
line 4.2: 'yarʿū al-zimām', literally 'they tend the rein (or halter)'; the idiom means they keep faith and hold to their duty.
line 4.4: 'fidākī', 'your ransom': we give ourselves for you.
